references.text: Israel is referred to as God's treasured people, a chosen nation among all peoples, reflecting the idea that the Lord took them to be His own people.
The Lord promised to take the Israelites as His people and be their God, and to bring them out of Egypt.
Solomon refers to Israel as God's people whom He brought out of Egypt, from the iron furnace, using the same imagery found in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah mentions the iron furnace as a symbol of slavery in Egypt when the Lord led the Israelites out.
Moses prays to God and refers to Israel as His people and His inheritance, whom He brought out of Egypt with great power.
Israel is a holy people for the Lord, chosen to be His treasured possession among all peoples on earth.
The Lord's portion is His people; Jacob is His allotted inheritance, emphasizing that Israel is God's heritage.
Believers are described as a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own possession—a New Testament fulfillment of Israel's calling.
